findings.action: Make the staged owner analyze index blobs, or fail closed whenever a selected staged path differs between index and worktree; add a regression test with unsafe staged bytes and clean working-tree bytes.
evidence: The hook derives names from the staged scope, but check_module_eviction_form.py reads selected paths from the working tree.

A developer can stage a test containing a forbidden sys.modules eviction, replace the working-tree version with clean content, and have the gate inspect the clean version while Git commits the unsafe staged blob.
The supplied tests do not cover index/worktree divergence.
findings.summary: The staged module-eviction gate can approve different bytes from those being committed.

findings.action: For the completed-lane persistence caller, require a well-formed explicit admitted path list and refuse malformed or absent classification. Keep stage-all only behind a separately explicit legacy API if still required, and add malformed-classification regression tests.

_commit_lane_snapshot stages every path when paths is None, so useful malformed candidates can commit out-of-scope residue instead of refusing.
The new tests cover valid lists but not missing, tuple, string, or otherwise malformed classification.
findings.summary: Completed-lane persistence retains an unscoped stage-all fallback when candidate scope metadata is missing or malformed.
